label: Qualifications & providers
title: Choose your course
description: Understand the levels and choose a suitable provider.
introduction: Compare the course, fees and campus before you apply.

sections.title: Qualification levels 1–10
sections.content:
New Zealand qualifications have 10 levels:

- Level 1: Certificate
- Level 2: Certificate
- Level 3: Certificate
- Level 4: Certificate
- Level 5: Certificate or diploma
- Level 6: Certificate or diploma
- Level 7: Diploma, bachelor's degree, graduate certificate or graduate diploma
- Level 8: Bachelor honours degree, postgraduate certificate or postgraduate diploma
- Level 9: Master's degree
- Level 10: Doctoral degree

A higher level means more advanced learning. The level does not tell you how many years a course takes.

sections.title: Where can you study?
sections.content:
- University: degree courses and research.
- Polytechnic or institute of technology: practical, applied learning.
- Private training establishment: specialist courses.

Check the exact course and qualification offered.

sections.title: Before choosing a course
sections.content:
- Does it match your previous study and career plans?
- What are the entry requirements?
- How long is the course?
- What are the total fees?
- Is practical training included?
- Does your future profession require registration?

label: Admission & scholarships
title: Apply for admission
description: Check the requirements, dates and scholarships.
introduction: Each provider sets its own admission requirements.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.content:
- Passport or other required identity document
- Academic transcripts and certificates
- Accepted English test result, if required
- Required translations
- References, portfolio or research proposal, if requested

Check how the provider assesses your Nepali qualification. English scores vary by course and provider.

sections.title: Dates to check
sections.content:
- Application deadline
- Course start date
- Offer acceptance deadline
- Deadline for meeting offer conditions
- Accommodation application date

Read your offer carefully. Ask the provider about anything unclear.

sections.title: Scholarship checklist
sections.content:
- Are applicants from Nepal eligible?
- Does it cover your course and study level?
- What grades are required?
- How much does it pay?
- When do applications close?
- Do you need a separate application?

Include a scholarship in your budget only once it is confirmed.

label: Study funding
title: Plan your study funds
description: Know how much you need and what evidence to prepare.
introduction: Budget in New Zealand dollars (NZD). Use your bank's current rate to convert to Nepali rupees (NPR).

sections.title: Minimum living funds for the visa
sections.content:
For self-funded tertiary study:

- Study of 1 year or more: NZD 20,000 per year.
- Study shorter than 1 year: NZD 1,667 per month.
- Extra: tuition fees and money to leave New Zealand.

Your actual living costs may be higher.

sections.title: Show where your money comes from
sections.content:
Prepare the evidence that fits your funding:

- Savings: bank statements and an explanation of large deposits.
- Education loan: loan terms and repayment evidence.
- Scholarship: confirmed award details.
- Family support: financial and relationship evidence.

Use Required Documents by Stage to organise your documents.

sections.title: Family support and tuition payment
sections.content:
For Nepali citizens applying from South Asia, eligible sponsors or financial undertakings are limited to immediate family:

- Partner
- Parents or parents-in-law
- Siblings
- Grandparents

Applicants outside New Zealand can choose to pay tuition after Approval in Principle (AIP). Keep the funds ready and follow the deadline in your AIP letter.

label: Visa preparation
title: Apply for your student visa
description: Follow the steps from offer to final visa.
introduction: Use the process stages to track your application.

sections.title: Your application steps
sections.content:
- 1. Apply for an offer.
- 2. Prepare visa documents, including medical and police evidence where required.
- 3. Lodge your visa application online.
- 4. Attend an interview if requested.
- 5. Receive Approval in Principle (AIP).
- 6. Pay tuition and submit payment evidence.
- 7. Wait for the final visa decision.

sections.title: Visa lodgement: fee and timing
sections.content:
- Application cost: from NZD 850.
- When to pay: when you lodge the visa application.
- When to apply: aim for 3 months before travel.
- Check the final charge for your nationality and application location.

Medical checks, police certificates, translations and insurance cost extra. Tuition is a separate payment.

sections.title: Interview: only if requested
sections.content:
Be ready to explain:

- Why you chose the course
- Your previous study and any gaps
- Who is paying and where the money comes from
- Your plans after graduation

Answer honestly. Reply to document requests by the stated deadline.

sections.title: After AIP
sections.content:
- Pay tuition by the deadline in your request.
- Submit the payment evidence.
- Wait for the final visa; AIP alone does not allow travel.
- Read the study, work and travel conditions on your eVisa.
- Arrange the required medical and travel insurance.

label: Living costs
title: Plan your living costs
description: A simple monthly budget for accommodation and everyday expenses.
introduction: All amounts are in NZD. These are 2026 Auckland examples; costs vary by city and housing.

sections.title: How much per month?
sections.content:
- Homestay with meals: about NZD 2,232.
- Student hall with meals: about NZD 2,492.
- Student hall without meals: about NZD 2,600–3,033.

These are total living budgets, including accommodation and ordinary daily expenses. Do not add rent again.

sections.title: What costs extra?
sections.content:
- Tuition and visa fees
- Flights and insurance
- Bond or advance rent
- Temporary accommodation and household setup

Check what meals and bills your accommodation includes before booking.

label: Arrival & student support
title: Get ready to arrive
description: Pack your documents and plan your first week.
introduction: Keep your passport, eVisa, offer, accommodation address and important contacts easy to reach.

sections.title: Before your flight
sections.content:
- Complete the New Zealand Traveller Declaration.
- Check the rules before packing food, plants or animal products.
- Clean used outdoor equipment.
- Declare biosecurity risk items when arriving.

Border officers decide which items can enter, even if declared.

sections.title: Your first week
sections.content:
- Complete enrolment and identity checks.
- Attend orientation.
- Check your timetable and route to campus.
- Find the international student office.
- Learn how to get academic and insurance support.

sections.title: If you need help
sections.content:
- Contact your provider's student support team.
- Ask about health, wellbeing and learning support.
- Use the provider's complaints process for concerns.
- If unresolved, check NZQA's guidance on external complaint options.

The pastoral care Code sets expectations for student safety and wellbeing.

label: Work during study
title: Work while studying
description: Check your work permission before starting a job.
introduction: Your eVisa tells you when and how much you can work.

sections.title: How many hours can you work?
sections.content:
- Eligible student visas: up to 25 hours per week.
- Full-time holiday work: only when your visa conditions allow it.
- Research master's and PhD students: may work unlimited hours while studying full-time.

The research rule does not automatically apply to taught master's courses. Follow the conditions on your own visa.

sections.title: Rules to follow
sections.content:
- Work for an employer with an employment agreement.
- Student visa work conditions do not allow self-employment.
- Check separate conditions for course-required practical experience.
- Resolve any missing or different work permission before starting.

sections.title: Before your first job
sections.content:
- Get an IRD number for tax.
- Keep your employment agreement and payslips.
- Track your work hours.
- Ask the careers team for CV and interview help.

Keep enough time for classes and assignments. Do not depend on finding work immediately.

label: After graduation
title: Plan life after study
description: Check your post-study work options early.
introduction: Your qualification and study duration affect eligibility.

sections.title: Post-Study Work Visa basics
sections.content:
- Length: up to 3 years, depending on your study.
- Degree level 7 or higher: generally at least 30 weeks of full-time study in New Zealand.
- Non-degree level 7 or lower: must meet the eligible-qualification list and related-job rules.

Check your exact qualification. The level alone does not guarantee a visa.

sections.title: Before your student visa expires
sections.content:
- Prepare proof that you completed your qualification.
- Check your application deadline; some study routes have different deadlines.
- Prepare at least NZD 5,000 in living funds for this visa.
- Keep valid immigration status.

sections.title: Upcoming change: 16 November 2026
sections.content:
Eligibility is due to expand for qualifying level 7 graduate diploma holders who also have a bachelor's degree.

This change is not yet in effect as of 14 September 2026. Check all conditions before relying on it.

sections.title: Choose your next step
sections.content:
- Look for work using your provider's careers service.
- Check professional registration requirements.
- Consider further study or returning home.

Work and residence applications have separate requirements. Graduation does not guarantee residence.
